 First snow, coldest air in months headed for eastern US in wake of storm
 By Meteorologists Dakota Smith , Chris Dolce , Briana Waxman 
 Updated Nov 11, 2026, 8:42 PM ET 
 PUBLISHED Nov 10, 2026, 8:54 AM ET 
 A weather model shows cold air plunging south across the eastern US. 
 CNN Weather 
 Extreme temperatures 
 Storms

 Tweet 
 Email 
 Link 
 Threads 
 Link Copied!
 Follow
 Winter will make its first cameo in the eastern United States this week as a storm ushers in the coldest temperatures in six months for tens of millions of people and the first snow for some.
 🥶 Get your local forecast and track the storm in the CNN Weather app 
 The storm will become a nor’easter when it reaches the Northeast coast, shaking up a period of relative tranquility in the region and becoming the first notable storm since September’s early season nor’easter .
 Nearly 200 million people east of the Mississippi will experience their coldest temperatures since spring as a tease of winter plunges south from Canada in the storm’s wake.
 Severe thunderstorms tracked through parts of the Ohio Valley Wednesday, producing gusty winds and quarter-sized hail.
 🌪️⚡️What makes a thunderstorm severe? More in the CNN Weather ap p 
 The storm’s blustery and wet conditions will spread into the Northeast on Thursday and then linger there through Friday.
 High elevations in the Interior Northeast are likely to experience their first snowfall of fall, and the lake-effect snow machine will also power on for the first time since spring in the Great Lakes.
 The storm’s expected path is now more confident, but forecast models disagree slightly on how much snow and rain will impact the Northeast and New England.
 Mountain snow and coastal rain
 Wet snow is expected in the mountains of the Interior Northeast southward through the central and southern Appalachians, especially Thursday night and Friday.
 Higher elevations of northern New England and upstate New York could receive at least a light coating of snow, which is most likely to stick overnight when temperatures are coldest.
 New York’s Adirondack Mountains and Vermont’s Green Mountains have the best shot at picking up more substantial snow, with totals ranging from 2 to 6 inches. The snow will be wet and heavy, so it could break tree limbs and cause isolated power outages in these areas.
 🌨️ ❄️ ‘Heart attack snow’ explained, only in the CNN Weather app . 🌨️❄️ 
 Some flakes could reach lower elevations of the Interior Northeast and mix in with the rain, but little accumulation is expected there.
 Along the Interstate 95 corridor from Philadelphia to Boston, the storm will primarily bring a classic autumn cold rain, which is expected to fall over a long enough stretch of time to limit the risk of flooding.
 Computer model forecast showing the timing and precipitation type for the storm. 
 CNN Weather 
 Breezy conditions will also swirl around the storm and minor coastal flooding is possible at times of high tide on Thursday and Friday from the New Jersey coast to southwest Connecticut.
 Cold is a lock
 Forecast high temperatures compared to average. 
 CNN Weather 
 Behind the storm, a brief cold plunge is set in stone for anyone east of the Mississippi River. Many areas will see their coldest weather since last spring as temperatures drop 5 to 15 degrees Fahrenheit below average.
 Sub-freezing temperatures are expected in parts of the Deep South overnight Friday and Saturday.
 Forecast morning low temperatures. 
 CNN Weather 
 For some in the South, the first freeze may arrive right on schedule as many areas, including Atlanta and Birmingham, Alabama, typically experience it during the first half of November.
 Parts of central Florida, like Orlando, could dip into the 40s for the first time since March.
 The cold will firmly settle in over the Midwest, from Minnesota to Ohio, preventing temperatures from climbing out of the 40s starting on Thursday and lasting through the weekend.
 This cold snap won’t have staying power.
 Above-average temperatures are expected to return next week in much of the nation’s eastern half. The mild temperatures could be preview of what’s to come in a winter dominated by Super El Niño .
 CNN meteorologists Taylor Ward and Tyler Ory contributed to this report.
